lens: all three in turn: learning-scientist, examiner, learner-advocate (scores below are per lens, then averaged)

gates.G3: pass. No validate output was available to the judge; S1 to S3 were read node by node in module.json and S4 to S6 were traced through the four sim walks (novice, misconceived, strong, guesser), each of which reached END with no dead end, loop or missing next. Not an exhaustive hand trace of every node.
gates.G4: pass. Every learner turn is a tap on a pre-written choice; no typed input; no run-time model.

coverage_note: Read in full: module.json nodes S1.start to S3.inv2c and the sign/coffee branches, the claim bank tail, and the report block. Read through sim walks and sim friction notes only: S4 management, S5 traps and the S6 cold check. Segment scores for S4 to S6 rest on those sources and should be re-checked by a judge that reads them node by node.

reasons.R1: Probe before explanation on almost every idea (S1.start, S1.both, S1.sort, S2.start, S2.why, S2.snd, S2.ile, S2.pain, S3.film, S3.num, S3.inv). Explanation is reached through a committed answer. Tell-only nodes are recaps and the S6 summary.
reasons.R2: Strong trap work. Wrong feedback follows Tempting, Why it fails, Right, with claims, and confident errors get sure_note branches (S1.expl_same, S2.a_x1, S3.film_xA, S3.caecum_x1). Pulled down by: S1.virgin's Crohn's option goes to a bare hint that never refutes it on first tap (only the retry reaches S1.expl_virgin_crohn); the S2.start_b, S2.snd_b and S2.pain_b re-asks repeat the same stem and options rather than a new form; S3.sign's plain-film options are dominated (see flaws).
reasons.R3: All twelve objectives are taught or tested on the main path and on the strong and guesser walks. O2 is non-core and gets two probes. The fast lane S2.a_ok skips the S2.why mechanism probe, so an expert on that path meets the level-timing mechanism only in the cold check.
reasons.R4: Probes are one question. Several feedback nodes stack three ideas or a 'Right:' clause inside wrong-answer feedback (S2.a_x1, S2.pain_x1, S2.cnot_x1). S1.both asks for a two-part pairing. S4.c5_p is hard to parse at speed (NOT question feedback). S5.richter_f_meckel opens with the wrong idea before correcting it.
reasons.R5: Fast lanes at S1.ok_both, S2.a_ok and S4.c1_ok. Hint ladder: Try again, then Show me why on some probes, and sure_note on confident errors. The second explanation is often the same stem re-asked (start_b, snd_b, pain_b), so remediation does not switch technique for most traps.
reasons.R6: The PYQ key versus current practice pairing (S1.both, TR1) is drilled as two columns. The test ladder, the 3-6-9 numbers, the 24/72-hour timings, the volvulus site rules and the strangulation override are all in exam form. Some re-tests repeat exam items verbatim rather than drilling new vignettes.
reasons.R7: Decisions in clinical moments: a dry adhesive patient, constant pain with tachycardia, a post-laparotomy patient on opioids, a 9-month-old, a stable caecal cancer. Vignettes are short but realistic.
reasons.R8: Warm and direct in the core probes. 'Tempting:' openers are a good voice. Pulled down by the drill feel of 'Same man, asked again' and 'Same high block, asked again' (identical options), 'Try again, or see why.' with no new cue, and a summary that promises cards the path never shows (S6.close).
reasons.R9: Each wrong option maps to one named trap and most feedback names the wrong model, so the path shows what a learner believes (the misconceived walk held beliefs in 20 of 20 traps; the novice and guesser walks show different profiles). Pulled down by report texts that do not match the walk: trap status counts first attempts only, so corrected retries are reported as fell_open (guesser); hinted_only is empty for the novice whose correct answers all came after hints; the misconceived walk's headline is 'mixed' in report.json but 'weak' in the sim note; and the strong walk's 39 of 39 cold check is praised without noting that it re-tests items already answered.

segments.reason: Best hook: the PYQ stem is committed before explanation, the teach-both pairing is taught with sure_note, and the sort and NOT forms are clean. Flaws: Crohn's option on S1.virgin gives a bare hint on first tap, and S1.virgin_b re-asks the same stem.

Richest feedback in the module: Tempting, Why it fails, Right, with claims and sure_notes, and the predict-then-show for level, sound and strangulation works. Flaws: three same-stem retry loops, a 'Right:' clause inside wrong-answer feedback, and the fast lane skips the S2.why mechanism.

Accurate and repetitive. Investigation of choice is asked three times in one segment (S3.inv, S3.inv2, S3.inv2c), signs are taught here and asked again in S5, S3.film2 keys on length, and S3.sign's distractors are wrong for an obvious reason so the key is findable by the enema modality.

Content of drip and suck, timings and override is good, but sims show confusing case order (c1_ok to c3 to c2 to c4), a NOT-question feedback (c5_p) that is hard to parse, and a vague hint (c6_h). Read via sims only; re-check node by node.

Good contrast pairs (femoral, Richter, Littre, Maydl, child versus adult, sigmoid versus caecal) but repeats S1 and S3 items verbatim (virgin case, coffee bean, claw and target, intussusception why), Richter feedback opens with the wrong idea, Littre feedback never names the right eponym, and hints are 'Try again, or see why.' with no cue.

Twelve consecutive quiz probes re-ask S1 to S5 items with the same options (about 36 to 40 steps of dead weight for a strong learner), the novice's S1 to S5 corrections are reversed by it, a fragment feedback (S6.q1_ok), and the walk ends at END with no card or report prompt despite S6.close promising cards.

best_parts: node S2.a_x1 and S2.a_x2: Tempting, then Why it fails with the level-based mechanism, then Right. Names the wrong model and refutes it with the repair. Graft this shape into S1.virgin's Crohn's option.
node S1.both with S1.expl_same and S1.expl_both_ca: the PYQ key and current practice held as two columns, with sure_note on the single-answer habit. Best treatment of TR1 in the module.
node S3.num_x6 and S3.caecum_x1: a calibre-based refutation that names the borrowed number ('you borrowed the colon's 6 cm'). Good error-type repair for E6.
node S2.cnot_ok and S2.pain_ok: the correct feedback for a NOT question explains why the finding fits simple obstruction, with claims. Good for a lucky guess.
report texts O3 'shaky' and O8 'gap': each names a derivation step and a concrete redo action (draw the timeline, trace bowel below the block).

flaws.problem: Crohn's option routes to S1.hint_virgin, a bare hint that never refutes Crohn's; the refutation (S1.expl_virgin_crohn) is reached only on the retry. A holder of the belief gets no correction on first tap.
Same stem and same options re-asked after a hint. Rubric asks for a delayed re-test in a different form; these are repeats, so a learner can pass by remembering the option text.

The two plain-film options are wrong for an obvious reason (claw and bird's beak are enema signs), so the key is the only pairing containing the enema modality. Dominated distractors (DP2): 'Bird's beak on plain film; target on ultrasound' loses every pairing.
The key 'Central loops, folds crossing the full width' is the longest option (DP1 telegraphing). Trim it to match.
Three investigation-of-choice probes in one segment; the second restates the first. One probe plus a ladder would test the same idea without repetition.
Wrong-answer feedback contains a 'Right:' clause that gives the answer inside a refutation message, so the tone flips mid-message and three ideas share one bubble (R4, R8).
The sigmoid volvulus distractor is mapped to TR18 (sound reversal), but it is a level and site confusion; the feedback (S2.ile_x2) explains sound, not volvulus. One error per option is blurred.
The fast lane skips the S2.why mechanism probe, the only probe of why constipation is late in high block on the main path. Experts on this path meet the mechanism only in the cold check.
Feedback opens 'Common slip: Richter's and Littre's are the same hernia' and then says they differ. The lead sentence states the wrong model as the correction.
Wrong-answer feedback for Littre's never names the right eponym, so the learner who chose wrong is left guessing.
Repeat S3.coffee and S3.sign almost verbatim with no new information. These re-tests should use a new form (e.g. image description or a management consequence).
NOT-question feedback says it 'is correct to name it as an indication' for the wrong option; hard to parse at speed (R4).
Hint is vague ('an action you take before deciding on theatre, step or decision') and gives no cue to the answer or the refutation.

Twelve consecutive quiz probes re-ask items already answered in S1 to S5 with the same options. Dead weight for a learner who has the answers; for a novice it reverses earlier corrections. Replace with 4 to 5 unaided vignettes in new forms (TR22, TR23, TR31 recur as the probe_plan says), and give a test-out fast lane.
Fragment 'none points to the hernial orifices first' does not confirm anything clearly.
Promises 'the cards that follow', but the walk ends at END with no card or report prompt on the path.

Trap status counts first attempts only, so corrected retries are reported as fell_open (guesser sim: TR2, TR4, TR13, TR21, TR36). The report should credit a corrected retry, or say that retries are excluded.

The novice walk got most correct answers after a hint, yet hinted_only is empty and the report says 'You used no hints' in spirit. The misconceived walk's headline is 'mixed' in report.json but 'weak' in the sim note; the sim and the report disagree and one of them is wrong.
'Cold check 39 of 39' is praised as a strength, though most of the cold check re-tests items already given. The report should say so or count only new-form items.

merge_ideas: S2's Tempting, Why it fails, Right feedback shape applied to S1.virgin's Crohn's option, so the first tap refutes the belief and the hint is the second layer.
S1.both's two-column teach-both probe with S2's predict-then-show, so the PYQ and current answers are held together and then tested in a clinical vignette.

Replace S6's twelve re-asks with five unaided vignettes in new forms (sign image description, timing sequence, first-step vignette, hernia comparison, intussusception contrast), keeping S5's contrast pairs as the source of the distractors.
S3's calibre ladder (S3.num_x6) and S3.caecum_x1 for the 3-6-9 numbers, plus one application stem in S6, so the number trap is taught once and tested once in a new form.
Report: credit corrected retries in trap status and count only new-form cold items in the cold-check strength line, so the path-based report matches what the learner actually did.

r9_report_check.method: Read sim/novice.report.json, sim/misconceived.report.json, sim/strong.report.json, sim/guesser.report.json and the sim .md reports.
r9_report_check.novice: Partly accurate. It names the right models (one answer per setting, fixed rules, look-alike signs, superlatives stretched). Misses that most hints were retries and that the S6 re-quiz reversed the earlier corrections, which is the thing this learner most needs to hear. 'Sure' texts describe answers never given.
r9_report_check.misconceived: Accurate about starting beliefs (overconfident, 24 wrong Sure taps). Not accurate about the end: every trap was corrected on re-test, yet the report still says several objectives are gaps (sim md says 'weak'; report.json says 'mixed' with all shaky). The text 'You are missing strangulation cues' describes the pre-correction state. The report should show that corrections held.
r9_report_check.strong: Accurate for the walk. Headline 'strong' and calibrated are correct. The 39 of 39 cold check is praised without noting that most of it re-tests items already answered. Useful card order.
r9_report_check.guesser: Calibration (underconfident) and fast lane are right. Trap statuses ignore corrected retries, and the O1 gap text overstates a gap the walk did not show (S1.both and S6.q1 were right first try). Next steps and card order are useful.

ranking: single module (round 1); no variants to rank
